_meta.purpose: Lamb regions and retail cuts. Seven regions match the master; USDA FSIS names five primals (shoulder, rack, shank/breast, loin, leg). Flank is kept as a region because the diagram and the retail cut both exist, with its FSIS parent stated.
_meta.scores_basis: tenderness_score 5 = most tender (loin, rack). richness_score 5 = fattiest (breast). Editorial.

regions.name: Shoulder
regions.short_description: Flavourful, fattier than leg, full of connective tissue. The American Lamb Board: requires low and slow.
regions.long_description: The Lamb Board describes the shoulder roast as the upper front shoulder, tougher and higher in fat than the leg, richer in flavour, less expensive and juicier. FSIS notes blade and arm chops from the shoulder are cheaper than loin or rib chops but may be just as tender. Smoked whole for pulling it follows shoulder logic; cut into chops it grills quickly.

retail_cuts.name: Shoulder roast (bone-in or BRT)
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: braise, roast or smoke; 5 to 7 lb; 20 to 35 minutes per pound depending on doneness for a sliced roast.

retail_cuts.name: Shoulder chops (blade, arm)
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: economical, quick. FSIS: may be as tender as loin chops.

retail_cuts.name: Stew and kabob meat
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: 1 to 1.5 inch cubes; kabobs to medium rare 145 F final; stew simmered 1.5 to 2 hours.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Pulled: roughly 1.5 hours per pound at 250 F. Sliced roast: Lamb Board 20 to 35 minutes per pound at 325 F. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: 30 to 60 minutes for a pulled shoulder; 10 minutes for a sliced roast.
regions.slice_direction: Against the grain (Lamb Board rule for all lamb); pull when at the tenderness window.
common_mistakes: Slicing a shoulder cooked to 160 F and calling it tough; it needed either less (145 F final) or far more (pulled).

regions.name: Rack
regions.short_description: The rib primal. Eight chops per rack (Lamb Board), nine ribs in the whole primal (FSIS). Tender, quick, the showpiece.
regions.long_description: FSIS: the rack is the primal cut more commonly known as the rib; it contains 9 full ribs and can be split into two rib roasts, and two roasts sewn into a circle make a crown roast. The Lamb Board sells it as eight chops, about 2 lb, Frenched or as a crown. Rib chops are, with loin chops, the most tender and most expensive (FSIS). Dry heat only.

retail_cuts.name: Rack of lamb (Frenched)
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: roast or grill, 9 to 12 minutes per pound to medium rare, 145 F final.

retail_cuts.name: Rib chops
retail_cuts.note: Cut between the bones; cook fast.

retail_cuts.name: Crown roast
retail_cuts.note: Two racks tied in a circle (FSIS).

regions.planning_time_guidance: Lamb Board: 9 to 12 minutes per pound for a rack, roast or grill. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: 5 to 10 minutes; the Lamb Board pulls 10 F under the target for carryover.
regions.slice_direction: Between the bones, against the grain.
common_mistakes: Cooking a rack to a shoulder temperature.
Not trimming the fat cap; it does not render in a fast cook.

regions.name: Loin
regions.short_description: Between rack and leg. Loin chops with the T-shaped bone; lean and tender.
regions.long_description: FSIS: loin chops come from the loin and, with rib chops, are the most tender and most expensive. The Lamb Board describes the loin chop as lean, tender, with a T-shaped bone, 3 to 4 oz a serving; grill, broil or pan-fry.

retail_cuts.name: Loin chops
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: 1 to 1.25 inch, 9 to 12 minutes, medium rare 145 F final.

retail_cuts.name: Loin roast / saddle
retail_cuts.note: Boneless loin rolled and tied roasts evenly.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Chops: 9 to 12 minutes total over direct heat (Lamb Board). Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Across the grain for a roast; chops are served whole.
common_mistakes: Overcooking; there is no fat to hide behind.

regions.name: Leg
regions.short_description: The hind leg. Lean, large, the classic roast; butterflied it grills; sirloin chops come off the top.
regions.long_description: The Lamb Board calls the boneless leg (BRT) the most versatile and the leanest cut, about 7 to 8 lb whole, most tender near the sirloin end; bone-in leg is the holiday roast. FSIS notes sirloin chops from the leg are cheaper than loin chops but may be as tender. The Lamb Board's time table: bone-in leg 5 to 7 lb at 325 F, 20 to 25 minutes per pound to medium rare (145 F final).

retail_cuts.name: Bone-in leg of lamb
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: 20 to 25 min/lb medium rare; 25 to 30 medium; 30 to 35 well, at 325 F.

retail_cuts.name: Boneless leg (BRT) / butterflied
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: leanest and most versatile. Butterflied on the grill is the backyard classic.

retail_cuts.name: Sirloin chops
retail_cuts.note: FSIS: from the leg; less expensive, may be just as tender.

retail_cuts.name: Leg steaks
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: 3/4 inch, 14 to 18 minutes under a broiler or on a grill.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Lamb Board and FSIS tables above. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: 15 to 20 minutes for a whole leg; pull 10 F under target (Lamb Board).
regions.slice_direction: Against the grain, parallel to the bone on a bone-in leg (Lamb Board: carve against the grain for the best texture).
common_mistakes: Cooking a lean leg to well done and wondering why it is dry.
Not tying a boneless leg; uneven thickness cooks unevenly.

regions.name: Breast
regions.short_description: The belly and lower ribs. Fatty, cheap, the source of lamb ribs and riblets. Braise or smoke low.
regions.long_description: FSIS groups shank and breast as one primal and lists rolled breast as a 1.5 to 2 hour braise. The Lamb Board calls lamb ribs cost-effective, marbled with fat, a substitute for pork ribs, for braising and grilling; its time table adds smoking. This is the fattiest lamb region and needs rendering time.

retail_cuts.name: Lamb ribs / Denver ribs
retail_cuts.note: Lamb Board: grill, roast or smoke. Render the fat; the bend test applies.

retail_cuts.name: Rolled breast
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: braise at 325 F, 1.5 to 2 hours.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 3 to 4 hours smoked at 250 F for ribs; 1.5 to 2 hours braised. Approximate.
common_mistakes: Pulling ribs early; unrendered lamb fat is unpleasant.

regions.name: Flank
regions.fsis_parent: shank/breast (flank is part of the breast plate; not an FSIS primal)
regions.short_description: The thin belly muscle behind the breast. Lean, coarse-grained; marinate, grill fast, slice thin.
regions.long_description: Not a separate FSIS primal; the Lamb Board's loin description notes the loin includes some flank meat and the rest sits with the breast. Kept as a region because the master diagram shows it and 'lamb flank' is a retail cut. Cook it like beef flank.

retail_cuts.name: Lamb flank
retail_cuts.note: Marinate, high heat, thin slices across the grain.

regions.name: Shank
regions.short_description: Fore and hind shanks. Collagen and bone; the Lamb Board: practically melt off the bone when slow cooked.
regions.long_description: FSIS planning: cover with liquid and simmer 1.5 to 2 hours. The Lamb Board: braise in simmering broth, 1 to 2 hours per pound, to medium (160 F) as a sliced target, though the point of a shank is to go well past that until it falls from the bone. Smoke first for an hour or two, then braise, and you have the best of both.
regions.planning_time_guidance: 1.5 to 2 hours simmering (FSIS); 1 to 2 hours per pound (Lamb Board). Approximate.
common_mistakes: Dry heat only; a shank needs liquid or a wrap.
